Situations / Surety Missing

Surety — Crown and Hollowell Search

Situation

The HCS Surety is in party hands. Crown administration has flagged the cutter as missing, Rupert Knighton has started a private revenge search for his dead son, and Verity Hollowell is quietly tracking the same disappearance because Geoffrey Draves was on the crew manifest.

Current State

The Crown clock started when the boarding ended. The party has roughly one month before Phase 3 watch notices harden around the Surety’s last logged description. Knighton’s private search is faster and less procedural. Verity’s search is quieter: she is using Hollowell secondary accounts and factor-network irregularity checks, not direct inquiries that would surface to her father.

World Tick — 2026-05-26: Beaumont arrived in Tidefall and gave testimony to Crown agents. The notice that went out carries the original description of the Uncertainty — already repainted, already wrong. Verity connected the Rook inquiry noise to her manifest gap and to Geoffrey. She has not reported yet. She is watching.

Toy Fields

FieldValue
VerbSearches. Three systems are looking for the same missing ship for different reasons.
Unstable ConditionRepaint and papers can beat port notices, but witnesses and factor gossip move faster than administration.
ConsequenceThe party may dodge the official watch list while still being exposed by Knighton, Beaumont, Verity, or the Hollowell ledgers.
Link of RelevanceThe Surety is the party’s ship; Geoffrey ties Verity to the crew; Rook and Cap’n Gorgeous tie Knighton to vengeance.

Key Facts

  • Missing is not lost. The Crown treats the first absence as paperwork, not emergency.
  • A repaint changes courtesy-stop recognition; it does not change cutter silhouette, wear pattern, or Crown interior fit-out.
  • False registry plate and defensible papers are the key inspection fix.
  • Knighton confirmed Cap’n Gorgeous’ death and sent one Knight into the Central Strait corridor.
  • Verity knows Geoffrey was aboard the Surety and that the ship went dark; Geoffrey does not know she knows.
  • A Hollowell bonded-cargo line moved through Tidefall without a formal manifest entry six weeks ago.

Crown Phases

Phase 1 (now to about 2 weeks): Port logs and waypoint inquiries; no active Crown search.

Phase 2 (about 2 weeks): Courtesy-stop notices begin if no contact. The notice describes the last logged Surety: naval grey, 80 ft patrol cutter, brass bow registry plate, Crown pennant, two cannon amidships, two swivel guns. Port Tidefall and Harwick receive automatically; Kalowe/Calveno only if remembered or escalated. Note: Beaumont’s testimony already went out carrying the post-repaint description — the Phase 2 notice starts wrong.

Phase 3 (about 1 month): Commander Gideon Ault aboard HCS Warrant is the most likely enforcement response. Authority includes detention, cargo seizure, crew arrest.

What Repaint Buys

Repaint plus false plate gets an unrecognized vessel into the water before the right description circulates. It does not hide the cutter hull form, patrol maintenance wear, boarding locker, brig cage, chart table, or officer’s aft cabin from a knowledgeable boarding officer.

Verity Hollowell

Verity Hollowell told Cedric about Geoffrey years ago and regrets the audience, not the disclosure. She has not accepted another arrangement despite Cedric’s introductions. She found Geoffrey on the Surety manifest and has not told her father.

Her ledger problem: Hollowell paperwork moved bonded cargo through Tidefall with no formal manifest entry. The paperwork is real; the gap is not an error. She has been deciding what to do for six weeks.

Hooks from Verity:

  • Ledger leverage against Crown inspection or unlicensed cargo movement
  • Hollowell pier scheduling access
  • Geoffrey returning to Tidefall
  • One introduced suitor with Admiralty connections

Involved Parties

  • HCS Surety — stolen Crown patrol cutter
  • Verity Hollowell — searching records for Geoffrey and sitting on a ledger problem
  • Cedric Hollowell — father, license holder, possible culprit or exploited authority
  • Commander Gideon Ault — Phase 3 enforcement; HCS Warrant
  • Beaumont Sel — living witness; has already testified in Tidefall

Triggers

  • Party enters a courtesy-stop port before repaint/papers
  • Knighton’s search finds a witness or vessel description
  • Verity connects Rook inquiries, the manifest gap, Geoffrey, and the missing Surety
  • Geoffrey returns to Tidefall

Blocks

  • Repaint plus removed/false registry plate before Phase 2 notices
  • Avoid major Crown ports until false papers are defensible
  • Keep Geoffrey away from Tidefall until the party understands Verity’s position
  • Use Hollowell ledger leverage before Cedric or Crown inspectors find the gap

Consequences

  • Good disguise before Phase 2: courtesy-stop officers look for the wrong ship (already partially achieved — Beaumont’s description is wrong)
  • No false plate: officers assess by eye and interior fit-out if boarded
  • Knighton gets a witness: private pursuit accelerates regardless of Crown clock
  • Verity engages first: party may gain pier scheduling access, ledger leverage, or a volatile Geoffrey scene
  • Ledger surfaces publicly: Hollowell license, Cedric, and Verity all come under Crown pressure

Open Questions

  • Does Beaumont reach Tidefall before the party gets papers? (Current: yes — already done)
  • Is Cedric responsible for the manifest gap or being used?
  • Does Verity protect Geoffrey, expose him, or use him to solve the ledger problem?
  • Which enforcement vessel receives the Surety tasking?

World Update — Session 03Roll: 8 — Partial. The Knight in the Central Strait picked up a merchant report matching Beaumont’s (wrong) description heading west. Investigated a different vessel — time wasted, but the Knight diverted further west toward Calveno’s waters. Closer to the party’s general area now, but searching for the wrong ship on the wrong description. No actionable intelligence gained.

World Update — Session 04 (Cold)

Roll: 15 — Partial Verity moved from watching to searching. She sent a discreet inquiry through Hollowell secondary accounts to a Midchain factor contact — asking not about Beaumont’s wrong description, but about the actual cutter silhouette: Crown-built patrol hull profile, 80-foot class, recently seen in Midchain or Central Strait ports. She knows what a Surety-class cutter looks like regardless of paint. The inquiry competed with routine Hollowell trade correspondence and didn’t get priority routing — it’s in the factor network, moving slowly, reaching Midchain contacts within the next week. The repaint buys nothing against someone searching for hull profile, not color. Hook strength: Ripple — a Hollowell factor in a port the party visits might ask about “a Crown-built cutter” in conversation that sounds commercial, not investigative.
